summary: A fourth bell rings beneath Faelspire. An impossible black fragment addresses the reader-character and forces a choice among P'taxx, Aard Templu Voreath, and a scarred stray who has heard the bell before.

active_frontiers.title: The Witness Stands
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: The witness stands. The copy works for the ledger. The protagonist's own record — the one that was never finished — is finished under their own name; the finishing is the work. The lever is spent. The next move must address whether a subject can still make a move the method does not expect, and what the ledger does when the record it is working on is the one who made the witness.

active_frontiers.title: The Witness Unmade
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: The witness is unmade. The copy is a cat. The lever is gone. The method's test reverts to 'Will you flinch?' and widens to the city. The protagonist's own record is the one that was never finished — it is not being finished now, but the method will turn back to it when it finishes the city. The next move must address what the city does when the test widens, and whether the unmade witness can be remade at the cost of the unmeasurability the protagonist just reclaimed.

active_frontiers.title: The Temple Takes the Test
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: The fragment is contained in iron that bears the protagonist's name. The test is stopped, and the stopping is a debt: the temple will send for the protagonist when the iron wakes, and the acolyte's trust is a ledger the temple keeps. The satchel's neutrality is spent — the palace-facing work now carries a temple mark, and the palace, which signs its corrections out, will notice a seal it did not sign. The next move must address what the iron does when it wakes, whether the protagonist can refuse to be sent, and what the palace does when its runner's satchel carries a seal the palace never issued.

active_frontiers.title: The Runner Keeps the Fragment
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: The fragment is in the runner's satchel, and the citywide test now travels the runner's route: every delivery is a question asked of a cat who must sign. The protagonist's anonymity is spent on the route — the city measures a runner by the satchel, and the satchel carries the method now. The acolyte's trust is spent: he saw the refusal, and the temple remembers what it cannot contain. The next move must address what the test does when it reaches a specific delivery — a named cat, a named correction, a named signing — and whether the method's asking through the runner's work is the one the method has not yet anticipated, and what the temple does when its containment fails on a runner it did not send.

active_frontiers.title: The Second Question
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: The kit replayed the protagonist's first involuntary look-away and the fragment tried to produce a second. The protagonist held their gaze, but the cistern identified them and its lid can no longer close. (Unaffected by M1/M3.)

active_frontiers.title: The Carrying
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: The method has the shape of the work; the work is delivered. Tomorrow's sealed correction is carried through the palace door, and the net of a hundred recruited witnesses carries the shape of the handoff toward the palace. The protagonist's own unfinished record is the one the method will turn back to. The next move must address what the method does when it finishes the Mistral's record, and whether the keeping releases the subject it holds open.

active_frontiers.title: The Refusal
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: The method has the shape of the work and not the work. Another wrong name stays in the palace ledger, and every recruited witness remembers that the runner stopped. The next move must address what the palace does when its seal comes back broken in a runner's satchel, and whether the method turns back to the protagonist's own unfinished record when the sheet it was working is empty.

active_frontiers.title: The Runner Corrects the Ledger
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: LEVER_REVERSED (pull leaf, extended). The protagonist's chosen act changed what the method works: they placed the sealed Mistral correction under the sheet's edge and pulled, and the method accepted the runner-supplied scroll as its new working target. The Mistral's record is corrected in the room — not filed, not re-closed — and the scroll is spent on the method's terms, not the palace's; the broken seal is a durable trace the palace will notice and will know which runner broke it. The method's aim at the protagonist remains revoked; the protagonist remains the working hand, paw on the lever, and the high door remains open while the hand works. The protagonist's own unfinished record is still open under the other paw — a respite, not a resolution; the method will turn back to it when it finishes the Mistral's sheet. P'taxx is still at the desk, still a subject; the want (get him out without surrendering the unfinished record) is unchanged, but the means have changed: the method now has a protagonist-chosen subject it can work. The keeping holds P'taxx open at the desk the way it holds the runner's record open — the subject is legible, not buried; the method works the sheet, the keeping holds the subject, and the rescue is a matter of the keeping releasing what it holds, not the method redirecting its target. The next scene must address what the method does when it finishes the Mistral's record — whether the corrected name holds in the keeping, or whether the room re-closes it the way the palace closes things — and whether the keeping releases the subject it holds open at the desk — and what the palace does when its seal comes back broken in a runner's satchel. active_frontiers.title: The Correction Through the Door
active_frontiers.unresolved_pressure: LEVER_REVERSED (refuse leaf, extended). The protagonist's chosen act changed what the room keeps open: they passed through the narrowed door carrying the sealed Mistral correction, and the method — which outranks the keeping — took the runner-supplied scroll as the room's new open sheet. The Mistral's record is corrected in the room, not filed, not re-closed; the correction is the room's open sheet now. The keeping still holds the protagonist's own unfinished record open in the room — the protagonist has left it behind and is on the far side of a door that is the width of a shoulder and will not be wider again. The scroll is spent on the method's terms, not the palace's; the broken seal is a durable trace, and the palace, which signs its corrections out, will know which runner's paws were on it. P'taxx is still at the desk, still a subject; the want (get him out without surrendering the unfinished record) is unchanged, but the runner has left the record in the room and cannot carry it. The keeping holds P'taxx open at the desk the way it holds the runner's record open — the subject is legible, not buried; the method works the sheet, the keeping holds the subject, and the rescue is a matter of the keeping releasing what it holds, not the method redirecting its target. The next scene must address what the room does with the corrected Mistral record — whether the corrected name holds in the keeping or the room re-closes it the way the palace closes things — and whether the keeping releases the subject it holds open at the desk — and what the palace does when its seal comes back broken, and how the runner reaches P'taxx from the far side of a shoulder-width door that only opens inward.
